title: A Learnable Bangladesh - real-world metas only

cards.a: "Indian" square roof tiles - "Indian" square roof tiles
cards.note: These square roof tiles (also common in West Bengal Indian) are found near the Western border with India, especially in Khulna division. Note: Contrary to the plonkit map used below, these can also be found in southern Rajshahi division and very rarely as far north as Rangpur division. They should still be clustered toward the Indian border in these divisions.

Barishal division uses architectural styles that separate it from other parts of Bangladesh. One of the most recognizable designs is this two-story house featuring separate roofs for the first and second floors. The lower floor is wider than the upper floor on both sides, creating a distinct "shoulder" shape. Use of exterior timber framing for this house style is also common. Look out for slight variations on this style which can also be clues for Barishal division and its surrounding area. Credit: "The Bangladesh Doc" by Radu C, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/u/1/d/e/2PACX-1vS6cGymuEpwoSaTI1BI7eteLSq5TlOo4Ky1GFFkN6lutRDua0nYJi95Yj-BZDKVTZxa38Ik96pf8cZH/pubhtml#gid=337612111
Beach sheoaks (Casuarina equisetifolia) are mostly found in coastal Chittagong, rarely in neighboring parts of Barishal division.

In southwest Dhaka, to the west of Kasiana, you can sometimes find large, bird-shaped adornments at the ends of roof ridges. (Note that simpler "wing-shaped" roof ridge endings are common in across most of Bangladesh; however, large, detailed bird figures with a distinct head should steer you toward this location.)

Chittagong division has by far the largest Buddhist population, so any present-day Buddhist temples/sites (not ancient ruins) are a decent clue for Chittagong. Note that Islam remains the majority religion in Chittagong—Buddhist presence is just larger and much more noticeable here than in other divisions. Hinduism is fairly evenly distributed as a minority religion throughout Bangladesh. Be careful not to confuse Hindu and Buddhist temples. Learning to recognize characteristic architecture (e.g. use of stupas) and iconography (e.g. the 8-spoked dharma wheel) can be helpful for differentiating them.
Yellow canola fields are usually found in Dhaka division.

cards.a: Chittagong Timber frame houses - Chittagong Timber frame houses
cards.note: Timber-frame houses in northwestern Chittagong division (the area surrounding Cumilla) have a number of distinctive features which help differentiate them from timber-frame houses in Dhaka division and elsewhere, including use of painted corrugated metals, panels with diagonally oriented corrugation, floral designs, and articulated wood frame shapes. See doc for detailed descriptions of these features, and more info on Bangladesh timber frame house distribution: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sezq-M_40qDTXgcXVo-OXnvA9mwBkL4mkiTPmWBTGP4/edit?tab=t.0

Larger cornfields are mostly found in the western divisions (Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna), more rarely in Myminsingh or Barishal. Tip: Look out for other evidence corn farming, such as piles of dried cornstalks which can be seen in towns even when cornfields are not visible.

Eucalyptus is mostly found in the north, especially Rangpur and northern Rajshahi or Myminsingh divisions. However, they can be found less commonly throughout Dhaka and Chittagong divisions. In and around Rangpur, it is common to find eucalyptus trees growing in rows along roadsides.
Orchards with neat rows of fruit trees such as mangoes are typically found in Rangpur and Rajshahi divisions, mostly near their northwest borders with India.

The border area between Magura (Khulna divison) and Kasiana (Dhaka division) features some very localized roof ridge ending styles. These harpoon-shaped roof ridges are more common on the Khulna side. They appear as a long metal extension overhanging the end of the roof, and will be notched on the bottom. (This region features a lot of particularly long pointed roof edges in general, but they are not a reliable regionguessing clue unless there are notches on the bottom giving the "harpoon" shape).

House-shaped haystacks are mostly found in the western divisions of Rajshahi and Khulna. Storing haystacks on roof-tops is also a common practice in this region. Note that the more dome-shaped haystack style seen elsewhere in the country can also be found here.
Hilly terrain can be found in parts of Sylhet and Chittagong divisions. The tallest, most impressive hills are found in the East and South of Chittagong division.
Western “hip” roofs predominate in the South and West of the country.

Mountain ridges to the north across the Indian border can rarely be seen along the northern edge of Sylhet. More rarely, similar ridges can be found in along the northern borders of Rangpur & Mymensingh.

Jute is mostly found growing in Rangpur division (NW Bangladesh), and less often in Rajshahi. See this link for a map showing other regions where jute might be seen: https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Jute#/media/File:JuteCultivationArea.jpg
In addition to jute fields, upright jute bundles with this shape are another common sight in Rangpur.

Although jute farming is most visible in Rangpur division, these loosely woven jute fences and walls can more often be found in Khulna and southern Dhaka divisions, especially along the border between the two.
These small structures with a conical metal roof are a type of traditional granary typically found mostly in Khulna, especially in the West of that division.

cards.a: Khulna mud houses - Khulna mud houses
cards.note: Mud structures in northern Khulna division often have this distinctive appearance, featuring a flat roof and pronounced horizontal ridges. Credit to Zetie from The Real Meta Research Group discord for identifying these as tobacco curing barns.

cards.a: Large triangular roof decoration - Large triangular roof decoration
cards.note: These large, triangular decorations on window roofs are found mainly northeast of Tangail within Dhaka division. Often white, but can be colorful as well. (Note that if you see one of these attachments on a house with exterior timber frames, you are likely to be south of the city of Dhaka.)

These distinctively-shaped boats are a very recognizable part of the cultural heritage of Cox's Bazar. They are sometimes seen displayed along the southern coast of Chittagong division, or can be encountered in actual use (rare on streetview).

cards.a: Mud houses  - Mud houses - Decorative lines
cards.note: Mud houses with decorative scoring, typically in arch or "scallop" shapes, can be seen in a small region south of the city of Bogura (Rajshahi division). The scoring is sometimes fairly faint and can be difficult to spot from a distance.

Mud houses can be found in the western divisions of Bangladesh. They are most densely concentrated in Rajshahi with significant numbers in northern Khulna and western Rangpur. Another pocket of mud houses can be found in south/central Chittagong, so check other clues such as roof type before guessing. Map credit: https://www.tslr.net/2007/07/mud-houses-of-bangladesh.html

A high density of pineapple fields in flat terrain can be found in NW Dhaka division and bordering areas of southern Myminsingh division. The area near Garobazar is especially dense with pineapple plantations, often growing alongside banana plantations (although bananas in general are more widespread found throughout the country). Note: Pineapple fields in hilly terrain are occasionally encountered in Sylhet and Chittagong divisions.

cards.a: Pointed ridge end with rings - Pointed ridge end with rings
cards.note: Throughout Bangladesh you can find examples of roofs with a protruding "point" at the end of the top ridge. Pointed roof ridges featuring one or more disc-shaped "rings" are useful for regionguessing. These roofs most often appear in Dhaka division south of the Padma River. Occasionally you will also find these in Rajshahi division, with some minor spillover in bordering Khulna division.
These tall green grass clusters are common to find lining roadsides in Rangpur division (NW Bangladesh). They may more rarely be found in other northern divisions of Bangladesh.

Rubber tree plantations are mostly found in hilly areas in the east, within Sylhet and Chittagong divisions. An easy way to recognize them is that they often (though not always) feature diagonal cuts along the trunks, resulting from the process of harvesting latex.

These relatively uniform forests dominated by sal trees (Shorea robusta) are common in the north central and northwest parts of Dhaka division. They should be found on flatter terrain. See the map/link below for a more precise distribution of sal forests in Bangladesh. Hillier terrain might help to differentiate Dhaka sal forests from those found in Sylhet. Credit: https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Map-showing-the-distribution-of-moist-deciduous-Sal-Shorea-robusta-forests-of_fig1_210196050

cards.a: Southern tree stands - Southern tree stands
cards.note: In the southern divisions of Bangladesh, you can often find this type of humid, dense, tightly-packed tree stands or forests. They often feature areca palms mixed with other narrow-trunked trees. This is particularly characteristic of Barishal, but can also be found in Khulna and Chittagong divisions. Note that you can still find plenty of other habitats, includnig wide-open crop fields, in each of these regions.
Sunflower fields are concentrated in southern Barishal division.

Sylhet division brick walls (NE of Bangladesh) often feature these distinctive bricks with letters on them. In general cement and brick walls are common in Sylhet division where fences might be used in other parts of Bangladesh.

Due to extreme weather, roofs carefully covered with tarp are a common sight in the Cox’s Bazar district in southern Chittagong division. (This is not 100% exclusive to Chittagong, so consider other clues).

Tea plantations are very common in southern Sylhet division, also fairly common in the rest of Sylhet and the part of Chittagong near the southern border of Tripura India. In these divisions, tea typically grows in sprawling plantations on hilly terrain, often raised above the road.

While tea is mostly found in the east of Bangladesh, tea can more rarely be encountered in northern Rangpur. Whereas the stereotypical tea plantation in Sylhet or Chittagong is sprawling and may or may not be hilly, tea plantations in Rangpur should be quite flat and may appear smaller in area. They should not be raised up above the height of the road. Credit: Atomo from "The Real Meta Research Group" Discord
The southernmost part of Chittagong division, roughly centered around Cox's Bazar, makes heavy use of these teal or turquoise metal roofs. Credit: Atomo from "The Real Meta Research Group" Discord

cards.a: Timber frame houses - Timber frame houses
cards.note: Timber frame houses are found in the South of Dhaka division, and to a lesser extent in Barishal division and bordering areas of Chittagong. In Dhaka division, they are often white, but they can also be painted in other solid colors or feature plain corrugated metal panels. Bonus: In many parts of Dhaka division you will see a mix of solid white panels and other types, but if you see only solid white panels all the way around the building, you are almost certainly in the area directly south of Dhaka city, along the Padma river. See doc for more on Bangladesh timber frame house distribution: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sezq-M_40qDTXgcXVo-OXnvA9mwBkL4mkiTPmWBTGP4/edit?tab=t.0
Tobacco is mostly grown in northern Khulna division, especially around the city of Kushtia.

cards.a: Vast rice fields - Vast rice fields
cards.note: An extremely vast landscape dominated by rice fields stretching to the horizon in found around the northeast corner of Dhaka division, and neighboring parts of Myminsingh and Sylhet, roughly centered around Mithamain.
Watermelon fields are concentrated in southern Barishal division.

cards.a: West Rajshahi pigeon pots - West Rajshahi pigeon pots
cards.note: Rows of pots hanging from the eaves of roofs are seen in the far west of Rajshahi division (NW of Rajshahi city). They mostly feature on two-story mud/clay houses. The pots are intended for pigeons to nest in.

In the western divisions of Rangpur, Rajshahi, and Khulna, this style of roof can be found, where the short end of the exterior wall extends in a triangle shape above the rooftop. (Note these roofs can rarely be found in other parts of Bangladesh, so check for other clues before guessing. Another notable cluster of similar roofs can be found along the eastern border with Tripura, India).

Eastern “window” roofs predominate in the North and East of the country. Note: In contrast to the plonkit guide map used below, this roof type was encountered routinely in Barishal division during creation of this map. It was still in the minority there, but it is not uncommon. However, it was practically never found in Khulna or Rajshahi divisions.

Timber framed top rows with a line of “X” panels across the top can be found west of Dhaka (city), just south of Savar. See doc for more on Bangladesh timber frame house distribution: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sezq-M_40qDTXgcXVo-OXnvA9mwBkL4mkiTPmWBTGP4/edit?tab=t.0
